newsitem.title: TURKEY: ISTANBUL STOCK MKT TO LIST HOSPITAL SHARES.
newsitem.headline: ISTANBUL STOCK MKT TO LIST HOSPITAL SHARES.

text.p: The Istanbul stock exchange said on Wednesday it would list partial shares of hospital Sevgi Ozel Saglik Hizmetleri A.S. on the national market on Thursday.
It said the opening price per 1,000 lira nominal valued share would be 9,000 lira. The company ric will be SVGSH.IS.

Sevgi became the first Turkish health institution to float part of its capital last week by offering 125 billion lira of new shares and 35 billion lira of old shares to the public when raising its capital to 825 billion lira from 700 billion.

Of the total 160 billion lira on offer, 104 billion lira worth shares were sold to 28 foreign institutional investors, 52.55 billion lira to 20,290 domestic individual buyers and 3.45 billion lira to nine domestic institutional investors.
Kleinworth Benson bought 15.5 billion lira, or 9.69 percent of the total offer, the Exchange reported.
The public share sale was managed by a consortium led by Turkey's Global Securities.

Sevgi hospital's major shareholder is Sevgi Yatirim Holding A.S. whose equity stake fell to 55.07 percent after the flotation from previous 64.91 percent. Orhan Ozcanl, owner of Sevgi Yatirim Holding holds a nine percent stake in Sevgi hospital, down from previous 13.44 percent.

The Ankara-based hospital, with a bed capacity of 65, reported net profits of 239 billion lira and net sales of 1.28 trillion lira in 1996, up sharply from 61.9 billion and 531.9 billion, respectively the previous year.
Its total assets surged to 1.57 trillion lira last year, from 663.4 billion in 1995.
The company earlier said income from the public offer would be used to finance a new hospital building project in Ankara.
